html:
US military program of 1966 to 1971 that lowered the mental and physical standards for new recruits, so that men who would have failed the entry tests could serve in the Vietnam War.

Robert McNamara, the defense secretary, launched it as part of President Lyndon Johnson's plans for a "Great Society". The stated aim was to give poor young men training and a path up, and, quietly, to find more soldiers without calling up more college students. About 100,000 men a year were meant to enter this way, and over 300,000 did by the end.

Critics called the men "McNamara's Morons". Many were Black or from poor families, and many were sent to combat roles. Studies disagree on whether they suffered higher casualties or gained from the training.

The program ended with the draft's decline in 1971.
sum: US military program of 1966 to 1971 that lowered the mental and physical standards for new recruits, so that men who would have failed the entry tests could serve in the Vietnam War.
